author: Nicole Brockbank
description: Self-described "Crypto King" Aiden Pleterski described how he tried to escape and how his alleged kidnappers ultimately released him during his continued testimony at their jury trial in Toronto on Monday.
title: 'Crypto King' Aiden Pleterski testifies about escape attempt during alleged kidnapping

author: Arturo Chang
description: A group of Manitobans doing volunteer work are back home after Friday's closure of U.S. airspace forced them on a long journey across that country.
title: Volunteers back in Manitoba after grounding of U.S. flights set them on long road trip home

author: Darren Major
description: Representatives from Meta say the social media company would have to "consider" pulling encryption services from Canada if the government's proposed lawful access bill passes without further changes.
title: Meta would 'consider' pulling services from Canada if lawful access bill passes as is

description: Andrew Chang explains the fight over what U.S. President Donald Trump calls 'Trash Island' — and why a federal judge blocked the Trump administration from closing Washington's historic East Potomac Park. Images provided by The Canadian Press, Reuters, Adobe Stock and Getty Images
title: The battle for Trump's 'Trash Island' golf course | About That

description: The 400 largest data centres in the United States put more heat-trapping gases into the atmosphere in one year than the entire nation of Denmark did, and that was before the artificial intelligence boom really got going, according to a Harvard University study published Monday.
title: Data centres in the U.S. put out more carbon emissions in a year than Denmark, says Harvard study

author: Candace Maracle
description: The father of a 16-year-old hockey player says he wants a public apology and cultural-competency training for the league after his son was the target of racist taunts at a tournament in Kitchener, Ont., on Nov. 8.
title: Father calls for apology after son target of racist taunts at Kitchener, Ont., hockey tournament

author: Sheena Goodyear
title: The U.K. is granting pardons to women for past abortion convictions

author: Murray Brewster
description: Canada's second-in-command is standing behind the proposed purchase of six Saab GlobalEye surveillance jets despite air force concerns about their capabilities. Vice-Admiral Angus Topshee told MPs he's satisfied with the procurement process, arguing the aircraft will contribute to an integrated continental defence network alongside satellites and ground-based radar systems.
title: Military's No. 2 defends GlobalEye surveillance jets despite capability concerns

description: United Airlines said Monday that it had resolved a technology issue that delayed departing flights, just days after a malfunction in the U.S. Federal Aviation Administration's network prompted a nationwide ground stop.
title: United Airlines says issue affecting departing flights has been resolved

author: Sara Jabakhanji
description: A Mexican journalist was found dead on Saturday on the outskirts of Acapulco, a popular resort city in the southern Guerrero state, marking the latest in a string of alleged attacks targeting reporters in the country.
title: Journalists call for justice after reporter found dead in Mexican coastal city of Acapulco

author: Ashley Fitzpatrick
description: Quebec Energy Minister Stéphane Paquet said the Churchill River power deal is not set in stone, setting off a series of questions for Premier Tony Wakeham in Newfoundland and Labrador's House of Assembly.
title: N.L. premier waiting to hear from Quebec on Churchill River power deal

author: Heather Kitching
description: The Gordie Howe International Bridge has seen more than a million crossings since it officially opened to vehicle traffic on July 27, according to new numbers from the Bridge and Tunnel Operators Association.
title: Gordie Howe bridge surpasses 1M vehicle crossings while other bridges, tunnel lose traffic

description: More parents are skipping vitamin K shots for newborns, but skipping it could lead to dangerous brain bleeds.
title: Parents are skipping vitamin K shots for newborns

author: Joel Dryden
description: Alberta’s controversial new riding map is one step closer to implementation after Justice Minister Mickey Amery tabled a bill in the legislature on Monday. But legal experts say a potential court challenge could introduce a high level of uncertainty in advance of the next provincial election.
title: Alberta has tabled a bill for new riding maps. What could a court challenge mean?

author: Kate McKenna
description: Sources tell CBC News five members of the Opposition leader's office have informed Conservative Leader Pierre Poilievre they plan to quit. The departures will leave big gaps in Poilievre's office, particularly in communications and policy.
title: Exodus in Poilievre's office as 5 staffers plan departures

author: Chris Iorfida
description: The U.S. Supreme Court made at least two significant rulings to shape immigration policy last year. In the coming months, there will at least three more opinions that could be impactful, as U.S. President Donald Trump's administration seeks to reinterpret a number of laws concerning asylum, deportations and the detention of unauthorized persons i
title: U.S. Supreme Court set to hear 3 major Trump agenda immigration cases

description: Hilda Svensson scored the decisive shootout goal and Sweden medalled at the women's world hockey championship for the first time since 2007 by defeating Finland 2-1 in the bronze medal final on Monday in Herning, Denmark.
title: Swedish women grab world hockey bronze from Finland, its first medal at tourney since 2007

description: The Trump administration on Monday issued a rule that will further restrict China's access to the best AI chips from companies like Nvidia, just as U.S. President Donald Trump began a trip to China to meet with President Xi Jinping.
title: U.S. further restricts China's access to AI chips in wake of Nvidia scandal

description: Toronto police say one man has been arrested in connection with a violent home invasion last month in the city's Bridle Path neighbourhood.

title: Silicon Valley leaders call for reinstatement of Nvidia CEO with 'Stand With Jensen' petition

author: Jeff Lagerquist
description: Bank of Canada governor Tiff Macklem will not seek a second term leading Canada's central bank. His current term as governor will end on June 2, 2027.

description: The national inflation rate was flat on an annualized basis in October, according to data released by Statistics Canada on Monday.

Carney says Canada could turn to Chinese automakers if Trump trade talks fail

title: Australian MP Helen Haines leaves hospital after losing both legs in car attack

description: The Canadian lobster industry is thinking of ways to recapture the Chinese market after competitors took advantage of retaliatory tariffs. Vietnam in particular was able to position its lobster well in 2025, filling the gap Canada left and becoming a strong competitor.

author: Leila Beaudoin
description: With the latest estimates putting the North Atlantic right whale population at just 382, a consortium is calling for urgent action to safeguard the species' survival.

author: Patrick Butler
description: The ophthalmologist who was Newfoundland and Labrador's top-billing doctor for the last two years straight is being sued by two former patients, including one who says his right eye was completely blinded during a botched cataract surgery.

author: Jackson Weaver
description: Nominations for the 69th Grammy Awards are scheduled to be announced today, broadcast live from New York's Time Square on Grammy.com and the Grammys' YouTube channel.

author: Alexandra Mae Jones
description: Canada took centre stage at COP31 last week to showcase its track record on cutting methane emissions. But some experts say the country can't be a global leader on reducing methane until Alberta, Canada's largest oil and gas producer, updates its equivalent regulations.

author: Daniel Leblanc
description: The Canada Border Services Agency has informed 63 employees that they will have to take on new, lower-paid positions because of medical conditions that prevent them from carrying a sidearm.

author: Sarah Law
description: A coroner’s inquest into the death of a 29-year-old Alberta woman at Lake of the Woods District Hospital (LWDH) in Kenora, Ont., is expected to start later Monday morning. Here is what we know about the upcoming proceedings.
title: Coroner's inquest into First Nation women's death in Kenora, Ont., slated to start today

author: Benjamin Shingler
description: At Quebec's provincial police academy, aspiring officers spend hundreds of hours on technical skills crucial to the job, from firing weapons to physically restraining suspects. Far less of their time explicitly addresses issues such as racial profiling and ethical breaches — which led to the firing of seven Montreal police officers earlier this month.

description: On Jan. 1, Kenny MacDonald set a goal to play 365 recreational sport games in Ottawa before the year came to a close. On Sunday, he completed his mission at the Bell Sensplex in Kanata. The CBC's Emma Weller was there.

description: Montreal students are denouncing the Service de police de la Ville de Montréal (SPVM) for what they call unjustified acts of violence during a protest against education austerity that took place on Friday.
title: Montreal students reeling from police violence at Nov. 13 education austerity protest

author: Kevin Maimann
description: As the UN prepares to discuss autonomous weapons this week, insiders say hopes of meaningful, binding regulations around AI in warfare are slim — and time may be running out.
